races.name: John Ormonde Wexford Sand Irish EBF (C & G) Maiden
Newtownanner Stud Irish EBF Stakes (Group 3)

runners_data.name: Ballyskeagh
runners_data.note: OR=120 juvenile who broke a maiden over 7f on good ground at Galway on last start, trained by JP O'Brien with a strong 13/77 fortnight; steps up to 1m here as a confirmed front-runner and likely to press hard for supremacy from the gates — gets this trip on a strong gallop is the key question.
runners_data.comment: Ballyskeagh won last time out but was fifth two starts back, giving her a mixed recent profile; she has run over today's trip and going before, though 44 days off and a 128 lb burden are tests of whether that winning fitness has been maintained.

runners_data.name: Bellesque
runners_data.note: Won over 1m on good ground and placed twice at 7f-8f, giving her solid credentials for this trip and conditions; confirmed pace-setter who will attempt to cross from her wide draw and find a lead, but with two equally determined rivals she may face a costly fight for the front rather than a clean bowl.
runners_data.comment: Placed third last time out after winning two starts back, Bellesque arrives on a fair fitness gap of 22 days with experience of today's trip and going in her favour, and carries 128 lb from stall 10.

runners_data.name: Damsel In Distress
runners_data.note: Prominent runner in the care of McLoughlin (T14: 0/19) who won impressively over 1m on good ground at Gowran 15 days ago; the short turnaround for a two-year-old filly is worth monitoring, and she will face stiff competition for the prominent ground given the traffic dangers two to three furlongs out.
runners_data.comment: Damsel In Distress arrives here in fine fettle just 15 days on from a winning effort, and she has experience of today's trip and conditions; a fourth last time out is the only blemish, and at 128 lb our top-rated runner looks the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Exceptionally
runners_data.note: OR=120 front-runner for AP O'Brien and Lordan whose recent form shows three runs without a win, including two thirds in Group company on good ground over 7f-8f; sets the pace here alongside Ballyskeagh and Bellesque, and her ability to sustain speed over the full mile after a contested early sectional is the crux of her chance.
runners_data.comment: Twice third in her last three starts, Exceptionally arrives here in good order on 20 days' rest and has run over today's trip and going before, but she remains yet to win in recent starts and her rating of 90 leaves her mid-pack against this field.

runners_data.name: Samnina
runners_data.note: Smart two-year-old for Mrs Harrington who won over 7f and finished fourth at the same trip, both on good ground; Shane Foley rides and she has shown the ability to travel prominently before quickening — the type who could benefit enormously if she lands a clean run two out amid the prominent-sector congestion.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of the field on our figures and with a modest speed rating of 77, Samnina is hard to fancy despite winning last time out; she has run over today's trip and going before, and at least comes here fresh from stall two.

runners_data.name: Sea Of Rain
runners_data.note: Consistent filly with six runs on good ground and solid placed form at 7f-8f, but her natural prominent style cannot be reproduced here given four rivals ahead of her fighting for those spots; Colin Keane is a high-class pilot who will make the best of wherever she settles, but the style displacement is real and tempers expectations in a shape that requires her to race as a hold-up type she fundamentally is not.
runners_data.comment: Sea Of Rain brings strong claims on the back of a win two starts back and a sequence of placed efforts in recent starts, and she has experience of both today's trip and going; the fourth last time out is the one blemish to address.

runners_data.name: So Lovely
runners_data.note: Arrives on the back of a win 9 days ago, a very short turnaround, but Ryan Moore takes the ride for AP O'Brien and her form of 2-2-1 at 7f on good ground is excellent; a natural prominent runner who has finished second twice before winning, suggesting she handles competition for position — one of the more naturally suited profiles for this strong-pace scenario.
runners_data.comment: So Lovely arrives in cracking nick, a winner last time out and placed in each of her two starts before that, and she has experience of both today's trip and the going; the chief concern is whether 128 lb from stall seven will blunt that momentum.

runners_data.name: Speckles
runners_data.note: AP O'Brien's third string here with form of 6-2, both runs on good ground at 7f, placing once; Ronan Whelan rides and she steps up to 1m for the first time, making the trip an open question — a prominent runner who will be swallowed up by the prominent pack and needs to find a way through the expected traffic.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last two starts, with a sixth two starts back undermining confidence, Speckles faces a stiff task on these figures, though a return to a familiar trip and a run just 20 days ago at least leaves her fit and ready.

runners_data.name: Sword Of State
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner for Brendan Duke (T14: 0/4) whose form of 7-1-8 is erratic — won over 7f on good ground but then finished eighth; Rory Cleary will have to thread through from the back of the field if the pace burns up, and the trainer's quiet book makes this a speculative outsider rather than a live player.
runners_data.comment: Sword Of State won one start back but has since finished eighth, and with a speed rating of just 59 she ranks eighth of ten on our figures, making her hard to fancy despite having run over today's trip and going and returning quickly enough on an 11-day turnaround.

runners_data.name: Tosca No Candis
runners_data.note: Won over 6f on standard-to-slow last time but her previous three runs show consecutive fifths at 7f-8f on good ground — a worry for both the trip and the going; WJ Lee rides for De Aguiar (T14: 3/13) and as a hold-up type, she needs the pace to destroy itself for her late effort to land.
runners_data.comment: Tosca No Candis arrives on the back of a win last time out and gets in from stall one carrying 128 lb, with experience over today's trip and going working in her favour; the risk is that three of her four recent starts ended in fifth.

races.paceDynamic: Three confirmed front-runners — Exceptionally, Ballyskeagh, and Bellesque — ensure this 1m Group 3 on good ground will be run at a genuine, unrelenting gallop from the outset, with all three likely to press hard for the lead and create a punishing early tempo. That sustained pressure will stretch the field significantly, making this a stamina-sapping test despite the flat mile at the Curragh, and is likely to set the race up for horses who can travel comfortably in behind before producing a sustained finish rather than a sprint. Prominent runners Samnina, So Lovely, Damsel In Distress, and Speckles will all be competing for the same ground just off the pace, creating significant congestion and traffic risk two to three furlongs out — horses who can quicken through gaps will hold a clear advantage over those needing a clear run from early. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than the map can accommodate, and of the three pace-setters, Ballyskeagh and Exceptionally — both rated OR=120 and handled with intent — are most likely to actually dictate, with Bellesque a shade less certain to find a clean lead. This race shape strongly favours a horse able to travel in a good prominent position without burning petrol early, then sustain a finish under the pressure of a genuine gallop — efficient, relaxed prominent movers who stay well will have the clearest path to victory.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Strong Pace, Stamina Wins
scenarios.trigger: If the three front-runners burn each other off and the race becomes a true test of staying power at the business end.
scenarios.body: Ballyskeagh, Exceptionally, and Bellesque fight out a fierce early gallop that stretches the field by halfway, meaning only those who have settled and saved energy can sustain a run; the final two furlongs become a battle of reserves rather than a sprint. So Lovely and Samnina, both prominent types who have shown the ability to win off strong paces at 7f-8f on good ground, are ideally placed to pick up the pieces from a position just off the leaders.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Clears Field
scenarios.trigger: If one of the pace trio — most likely Ballyskeagh or Exceptionally — gets a soft lead while the others concede position and settles into a controlled rhythm.
scenarios.body: A well-rated front-runner who avoids a full-blown pace battle can dictate terms, avoid the prominent-sector congestion entirely, and produce enough of a quicken in the straight to hold on as the closers arrive late. Ballyskeagh, who won over 7f on good ground last time and steps up in trip, or Exceptionally, experienced in Group company, could exploit this if rivals take each other on.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Traffic Chaos, Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent pack of four gets bunched and squeezed two to three furlongs out, creating a logjam that benefits the freshest closer.
scenarios.body: The congestion among Samnina, Speckles, So Lovely, Damsel In Distress, and the redistributed Sea Of Rain — who will struggle to reach a natural prominent berth — creates a chaotic mid-race where gaps close and horses check, leaving daylight only for those widest or most patient. Tosca No Candis, a hold-up type who won last time and handles good ground, and Sword Of State, despite inconsistency, both have the profile to storm home late if the pace truly burns up.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Midfield Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace proves unsustainably fast and front-runners tie up dramatically inside the final two furlongs, handing the race to a midfield mover.
scenarios.body: An extreme scenario where all three pace-setters exhaust each other and the trailing pack simply runs past them; good ground at the Curragh is unlikely to punish pace that severely, making this the least probable shape. Sea Of Rain, a genuinely prominent horse racing out of role in midfield with a STYLE_FIT of 0.92 and inconsistent form at this level, would need everything to fall perfectly for this to benefit the hold-up contingent.

watchPoints.text: Prominent sector congestion — Samnina, So Lovely, Damsel In Distress, and Speckles all want the same ground just off the pace; watch for checks, switching, and lost momentum two to three furlongs out as this is where the race is most likely to be won or lost for the chasing pack.

Bellesque's wide draw could compromise her ability to cross and lead cleanly; if Exceptionally and Ballyskeagh pin her wide from the gates, she may burn significant early energy fighting for position rather than controlling the tempo.

Sea Of Rain is a genuine prominent type who cannot get her position here and will be racing a full length of the straight out of role; Colin Keane's horsemanship may limit the damage but backers should be clear-eyed that her STYLE_FIT discount is meaningful in this shape.

So Lovely runs for the second time in nine days — a short turnaround for a two-year-old filly in a Group 3; she arrives in form but Ryan Moore will need to manage her energy carefully if she is to sustain a finish under a strong pace.

Sword Of State's trainer Brendan Duke holds only a 0/4 record over the last 14 days and the horse's form is highly inconsistent (7-1-8); monitor any market move as a directional signal, but the profile suggests he is best watched rather than backed in a race this competitive.

races.name: Audi Naas Nursery Handicap

runners_data.name: Tradewinds
runners_data.note: Natural front-runner for Donnacha Aidan O'Brien, ridden by claimer Paddy Harnett; has hit the board in five of six career starts on good ground but is yet to win, and faces the toughest pace test of his career here with two rivals equally intent on leading.|
runners_data.comment: Consistent profile with thirds two and three starts back, and a second four starts back, Tradewinds steps up with experience over today's trip and going, fit enough on 20 days' rest; yet to score in recent starts, but our rating of 93 marks him as one to take seriously from stall one.

runners_data.name: Banks Of The Boyne
runners_data.note: Won over this course and distance nine days ago for Michael Mulvany, giving this lightly raced handler a solid recent platform; a front-runner who gets first run on his rivals and whose course-and-distance win is the standout form piece in the field.|
runners_data.comment: Banks Of The Boyne arrives on the back of a win last time out and looks to have strong claims returning nine days later in fine form, having already encountered today's distance and going; the main risk is whether 137 lb blunts his momentum.

runners_data.name: Luca Brillante
runners_data.note: D K Weld's patient hold-up operator is running out of his natural style here — placed at 8f suggests stamina suits — and Chris Hayes has the tactical sense to get cover in a field full of pace, making this potentially the right race shape for a first win.|
runners_data.comment: Luca Brillante ran a solid second last time out and returns in good order after just 11 days, with experience of today's trip and conditions working in her favour; the worry is that she remains winless in recent starts and must prove she can go one better.

runners_data.name: Margot Mae
runners_data.note: Shane Foley takes the mount on this front-running filly who returns from a 51-day break for Mrs John Harrington; her form figures of 637 and no place on good ground are modest, and absence combined with high pace expectations makes her a significant pace-shape risk.|
runners_data.comment: Margot Mae shaped well when third two starts back and our rating has her marginally top of these rivals, but she has been winless in recent starts and 51 days off the track is a fitness query she must answer here.

runners_data.name: Elyatta
runners_data.note: Noel Meade's hold-up type wears a hood (tongue-tie) and is flagged for fading in finishes, which is a serious concern in a race likely to produce a sustained gallop that tests every runner's resolution; a string of single-figure finishes at both 6f and 8f on good ground offers little encouragement.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last three starts, with a pair of tail-end finishes his most recent efforts, Elyatta is hard to fancy on these figures despite having run over today's trip and going before; he carries 121 lb from stall five, and our rating of 75 leaves him well held among these.

runners_data.name: Exchange Student
runners_data.note: J A Stack's genuine rear-runner carries the lowest OR in the field and is mapped to midfield only because the pace contingent is too large; its true style is deep hold-up, and with a STYLE_FIT score of 0.90 indicating it is racing out of role, its chances of threading through in a hot-paced race are modest at best.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last four starts, Exchange Student heads into this rated just 55 officially and ranked last on our figures, making her hard to fancy; she does have experience over today's trip and going, and 24 days since her last run leaves her reasonably fresh.

races.paceDynamic: Tradewinds, Banks Of The Boyne, and Margot Mae are all confirmed front-runners in a six-runner field over 7f at the Curragh, making a strong, pressured gallop from the outset near-certain. With three horses competing for the same real estate in the first two furlongs, the pace will be genuine and sustained rather than tactical, stretching this field on good ground and placing a premium on stamina over raw speed. Luca Brillante and Exchange Student are both hold-up types, but Exchange Student — a genuine rear-runner — is shown in midfield on the map because the field contains more hold-up horses than the map can accommodate at the back; Banks Of The Boyne is best placed to actually control the front given a recent win over this course and distance. This shape strongly favours hold-up or late-finishing profiles that can be covered up while the pace hotpot burns itself out, then unleash a sustained run in the final two furlongs.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Strong Pace, Closers Prevail
scenarios.trigger: If the three front-runners cut each other's throats and the race falls apart for the pacesetters in the final furlong
scenarios.body: Tradewinds, Banks Of The Boyne, and Margot Mae set a relentless pace that grinds them all down inside the final furlong, handing the advantage to horses held up or tracking in midfield. Luca Brillante, switched off by Chris Hayes from a hold-up position, is best placed to reel in the leaders on this flat 7f track.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: One Pacemaker Clears Field
scenarios.trigger: If Banks Of The Boyne asserts early dominance and the other front-runners fail to match the tempo, allowing one leader to secure a clear, uncontested advantage
scenarios.body: Banks Of The Boyne, fresh off a course-and-distance win nine days ago, pushes to the front and sets a controlled but honest gallop, taking the sting out of rivals without over-extending. With the challengers scattered and the hold-up horses potentially left with too much ground to make up, Banks Of The Boyne's stamina and recent winning form see the race out.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Hold-Up Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the frantic early battle causes a dramatic fade from all three front-runners in the final 2f, creating a winning opportunity for the deepest-closing profiles
scenarios.body: A truly brutal early pace sees Tradewinds, Banks Of The Boyne, and Margot Mae all weakening at the two-pole, opening the door for any horse tracking just off the pace. Luca Brillante's sole placed run came at 8f on good ground, suggesting stamina is a strength, and a patient ride from Hayes could produce a strong late surge.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Modest Pace, Front Runners Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If two of the three pacemakers settle quickly behind one leader, producing a steadier tempo that fails to test stamina
scenarios.body: Should the pace be less fierce than expected — perhaps Margot Mae after a 51-day break fails to fire early — the front-runner(s) could dominate a muddling race that produces a sprint finish. Tradewinds or Banks Of The Boyne would be best suited, with stamina becoming irrelevant and early position decisive on a flat track.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Banks Of The Boyne or Tradewinds takes the early initiative — if one asserts clearly in the first furlong, the other two front-runners may ease back, transforming this from a suicidal pace duel into a controlled front-running race that suits the leader.|

Margot Mae returns from 51 days off and, if backward in condition, could drop away quickly after the early dash, creating a confusing positional shuffle behind the leaders that disrupts hold-up horses' runs.|

Exchange Student's true running position at the rear means Pietropaolo (7lb claimer) may find the horse boxed in or outrun early when the pace is strong; watch for signs of greenness or lack of response in the first two furlongs.|

Elyatta's finishing pattern — fading late — is particularly dangerous in what promises to be an end-to-end gallop; if she tires in the straight she could block or hamper hold-up runners making their challenge down the centre of the track.|

Luca Brillante's only placed run came at 8f, and this 7f trip on a flat Curragh track is notably shorter than his form peak; watch how far off the pace Hayes elects to travel, as too far back on a flat track with limited pace advantage in the final furlong could leave him with too much to do.|

races.name: Heider Family Stables Round Tower Stakes (Group 3)

runners_data.name: Great Barrier Reef
runners_data.note: Unbeaten in three starts all over 6f, two on Good, one on Soft, and Ryan Moore's booking for O'Brien's charge is a significant upgrade; has won here at the Curragh over this trip and simply needs to track Ruler's Control in his natural prominent position to be in the race until the very end.
runners_data.comment: Three wins in a row make Great Barrier Reef a compelling threat, and he has experience of both today's trip and going; the main concern is a 74-day absence since that last victory, with 136 lb to shoulder from stall five.

runners_data.name: Push The Boat Out
runners_data.note: Only has one run to his name but it was a striking 6f win on Good going, and Seamie Heffernan retaining the ride for the in-form M D O'Callaghan operation suggests connections are confident this sharp, prominent-racing type can step up to Group 3 company.
runners_data.comment: Push The Boat Out won last time out but ranks sixth of seven on our figures, with a speed rating of 75 doing little to inspire confidence at this level; he has run over today's trip and returns after 20 days, yet the weight of evidence makes him hard to fancy.

runners_data.name: Ruler's Control
runners_data.note: The confirmed front-runner here and will get a soft lead — the drop back from 7f to 6f is a positive given its early speed, though a rating of 100 means it will need to dictate perfectly and hope rivals don't quicken past it in the closing stages; no headgear concern but five-race mileage for a two-year-old worth monitoring.
runners_data.comment: Ruler's Control won three starts back and has since finished fourth and fifth, so he arrives here needing to recapture that form; experience over today's trip and going is in his favour, and he carries a workable 131 lb from stall one, but the five-week absence is the key question mark.

runners_data.name: Where Love Lives
runners_data.note: A hold-up type for Soumillon and Donnacha O'Brien, with form figures of 1-1-12-4 showing the defeats came on softer ground and in more pressured races; the likely sedate tempo here is the primary concern, as Where Love Lives needs a strong pace to generate the late momentum that delivered earlier wins.
runners_data.comment: Where Love Lives won on each of his last two winning starts — victories three and four starts back — and arrives here fit enough on 30 days' rest with experience of today's trip and going; the concern is that he has finished outside the places in his two most recent outings.

runners_data.name: Beibhinn
runners_data.note: Has shown genuine ability winning over 6f on Good at the Curragh but has hit a flat patch of form (3-3-6 in last three); by nature a forward-racing type, she is likely to find prominent positions taken by higher-rated rivals ahead of her and the style-fit discount of 0.93 is a realistic reflection of how compromised her race may be.
runners_data.comment: Placed third on two of her last four starts and a winner four starts back, Beibhinn has experience of today's trip and going in her favour, though that sixth last time out and a mid-division draw 6 suggest she faces a stiff task off 128 lb against stronger rivals.

runners_data.name: Livenka
runners_data.note: Won back-to-back 6f races on Good going to earn this Group 3 pitch and Colin Keane keeps the ride, which is an important positive; however, her natural prominent style is likely to be squeezed out by the volume of forward runners, and the four-from-four form on Good is tempered by the 0.92 style-fit flag suggesting she may not get the run of this race.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Livenka faces a stiff ask off 128 lb, and a 17-lb gap between her official mark and our rating is a real concern; in her favour, she has winning form in her last four starts and experience over today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: Velozee
runners_data.note: A prominent racer with a mixed recent record (3-3-8-4-3 in last five on Good) but rated 108 and Pat Twomey's runner carries experience; the trainer's 14-day record of 0 winners from 14 is a note of caution, and Velozee will need to produce a career-best to threaten the higher-class rivals if the pace is controlled.
runners_data.comment: Velozee arrives here in sound shape just 20 days after her latest third, has experience of today's trip and going, and with two wins in her last six starts she carries plenty of class into this; the 128 lb burden is the one query, but on a rating of 111 she heads these rivals.

races.paceDynamic: Ruler's Control is the sole confirmed front-runner in this seven-runner Group 3 6f contest and should be allowed to stride into a clear lead from the outset, setting a sustainable but not pressured gallop on Good turf at the Curragh. Great Barrier Reef, Push The Boat Out, and Velozee will all look to press or track closely in the prominent positions, creating a compact, controlled early tempo rather than a searching pace test. The field holds more prominent-style runners than the race shape can accommodate — Livenka and Beibhinn are genuine prominent types who, given the volume of horses wanting to race forward, are more likely to be shuffled back into a midfield role than to secure their natural position. With a single unhurried pace-setter and a cluster of prominent types travelling smoothly just behind, this race shape most favours horses who can race in the first two or three early and then sustain their effort through the final two furlongs — a clean, front-to-prominent running profile is the clear beneficiary on this configuration.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Ruler's Control Dictates Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Ruler's Control leads unchallenged at a measured gallop and the prominent chasers are unable to reel it in inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Ruler's Control bowls along uncontested, the pace stays honest but not brutal, and those tracking closely — Great Barrier Reef and Push The Boat Out — get the ideal draw on its heels to mount late challenges; the winner comes from the front two or three with minimal fuss.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is just strong enough to stop Ruler's Control holding on and one of the close-tracking prominent horses (Velozee or Great Barrier Reef) picks them off inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: A fraction more urgency in the middle stages stretches the field sufficiently that the horse sitting second or third with a cover of pace makes a decisive move at the two-furlong pole; the sustained 6f on Good turf at Curragh rewards the type who relaxes early then finds a gear.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Redistributed Prominent Bursts Through
scenarios.trigger: If Livenka or Beibhinn, unable to find their natural prominent slot, get a smooth run through midfield and benefit from a gap appearing in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Racing wide or through horses, one of these naturally forward-going types finds a split late and their raw ability compensates for the compromised position; however, both carry a style-fit discount and this shape depends on things going wrong for those ahead.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Lands Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong and Where Love Lives, held up off a fast gallop, produces a sustained late run from the rear.
scenarios.body: Where Love Lives has winning form over course and distance on Good and Soumillon could angle a late challenge if the gallop has strung the field out; however, this race shape looks too sedate and controllable for a hold-up horse to get a meaningful tow into the race.

watchPoints.text: Ruler's Control is the sole front-runner — if it is allowed to bowl along unopposed in front, the race effectively runs to suit whoever is sitting closest to it, and any traffic or interference behind it could prove decisive for the prominent chasers.

Livenka and Beibhinn are both natural prominent types likely to find their forward position taken — watch their starting positions and early strides closely, as any scrimmaging for the prominent slots in the first furlong could compromise both runners significantly.

Push The Boat Out has only one career run — while that debut win was impressive, this is a significant rise in class and the unknown quantity of how it handles race-day pressure in a Group 3 field is a genuine variable on its chance.

Great Barrier Reef steps up in class on the back of three wins but comes here after a 74-day absence — watch how sharply it travels in the early stages, as a prominent type returning from a layoff may take a furlong to find its stride before engaging.

The Going is Good throughout the card with no notable variation — no runner has a meaningful surface edge over another, meaning class and tactical position will be the determining factors rather than any going preference.

races.name: Snow Fairy Fillies Stakes (Group 3)

runners_data.name: Bosphorus Rose
runners_data.note: Prominent-running 4yo for Pat Twomey who won over 12f on Good last time at this venue — stepping back in trip but the distance looks within range; 15 days since that win keeps freshness, though five placed efforts in six recent runs suggests she finds a way to finish without winning.
runners_data.comment: Bosphorus Rose won two starts back and was third three starts back, showing she can mix it at this level, but a fifth last time out gives pause; she has run over today's trip and going, carries 133 lb from stall nine, and returns after a brisk 15-day turnaround.

runners_data.name: Faiyum
runners_data.note: Front-runner with strong Good-ground form including two wins at this track; 116-day layoff is the headline concern for G M Lyons, though she has won fresh before and Colin Keane's booking suggests the stable is confident she comes to hand — she must take on Garden Party for supremacy early.
runners_data.comment: Faiyum won three starts back and was third two starts back, showing consistent recent form, and she has distance and going experience to call on; the concern is a 116-day absence carrying 133 lb from stall six.

runners_data.name: Princess Child
runners_data.note: A hold-up 5yo who carries headgear (t) and has been well beaten in three recent starts, form reading -72500; Scott McCullagh takes over and she steps back to 1m1f, but recent evidence offers little encouragement on Good ground at Curragh where she ran 8th of 15 last time.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Princess Child nonetheless brings strong distance and going experience to the table and her rating of 112 makes her a live threat in a field of 15; the risk is that her two most recent efforts were unplaced.

runners_data.name: Sindria
runners_data.note: Hold-up filly who has won twice in her last five starts and handles Good going well, sitting out 62 days here for Joseph O'Brien; her sim-going record (7/10) is middle-of-the-road but her best form — both wins — has come on Good or Soft, and Declan McDonogh knows how to deliver from this position.
runners_data.comment: Sindria showed smart form with back-to-back wins four and five starts back, and experience over today's trip and going underlines her claims under 133 lb from stall five; the main concern is that she was beaten into fifth last time out after a 62-day absence.

runners_data.name: Spicy Margarita
runners_data.note: OR 93 hold-up type whose true racing style is from the rear, though the density of hold-up horses in this field means she will likely find herself shuffled into a midfield berth that doesn't suit; her recent record (0W0P, 11/15 in similar going) is not encouraging and the redistribution diminishes her chance.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Spicy Margarita nevertheless holds a rating edge over her official mark and has experience of today's trip and conditions, though a fourth is her best recent effort and she carries 133 lb from stall two after a 35-day break.

runners_data.name: Syzygy
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer with recent hurdles experience (hg:p), last run only 8 days ago for Daniel McLoughlin — that quick turnaround is worth noting on Good ground; has placed twice in five recent Good-ground outings but is yet to win, and the 1m1f will suit her staying profile if Ben Coen can find a clear run.
runners_data.comment: Syzygy shaped with promise when a second three starts back, and she has experience over today's trip and going, but winless in her last six starts and that ninth last time out raises questions she must answer from stall 10 carrying 133 lb.

runners_data.name: Thalara
runners_data.note: 6yo prominent runner returning after 343 days off for Henry De Bromhead — a massive layoff is the dominant concern despite an excellent record of 2W5P in the last five Good-ground starts including a win over 1m; the 8/34 T14 strike rate suggests De Bromhead returns horses ready, but this distance of absence demands scrutiny.
runners_data.comment: Thalara was a winner two starts back and has placed on three other recent occasions, but she returns from a 343-day absence and an unplaced effort last time gives her something to prove; she has run over today's distance and going before and carries 133 lb from stall seven.

runners_data.name: Della Pace
runners_data.note: 3yo filly whose best position is off the pace from the hold-up berth, but the surplus of back-markers in this field means she is effectively filling a midfield slot out of role; her form of 5-2434 shows consistent placing without winning, and Ronan Whelan will need a clean run through traffic at 1m1f for the first time.

runners_data.name: Drop Dead Gorgeous
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore takes over this A P O'Brien 3yo who won over 1m on Soft last time; carries the hg:t flag and has run at 1m consistently, so the extra furlong here is a step into the unknown — but the Moore booking in a Group 3 is a powerful signal and her hold-up style is ideally suited to a pace-pressured race.
runners_data.comment: Ranked 11 of 15 on our figures, Drop Dead Gorgeous has shaped poorly in her last three starts, finishing eighth, fifth, and ninth, and the return after 45 days adds an element of doubt; a win five starts back and experience over today's trip and going are slim comfort.

runners_data.name: Garden Party
runners_data.note: A P O'Brien's lightly-raced 3yo who has won once and placed twice in all three starts — all at this trip or beyond — and heads here fresh (15 days); she will dispute the lead with Faiyum throughout, and whether she can sustain that battle over 1m1f on Good is the question given her limited experience.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of the field on our figures with a speed rating of 66, Garden Party faces a stiff ask here, though she does arrive on the back of a win last time out, has experience of today's going, and is fit enough on a 15-day turnaround.

runners_data.name: Meriden
runners_data.note: Denis Hogan's progressive 3yo has won four of her last five and is unbeaten in all six completed runs, with a 2nd the only blemish; she wants to race prominently and handles Good ground well (5/10 in similar conditions), though she steps up sharply in class here and is moving from 6-8f to 1m1f for the first time.
runners_data.comment: Meriden arrives on the back of fine recent form, winning five of her last six starts and finishing second last time out, with experience over today's distance and going in her favour; 126 lb and stall 13 are the questions she must answer.

runners_data.name: Miss Scott
runners_data.note: John & Thady Gosden send this 3yo across with Christophe Soumillon aboard — a significant jockey booking — after two wins at 1m on Good and Soft; she races prominently and has placed in all four career starts, but has not raced beyond 10f, making this 1m1f assignment and a first trip to Curragh a dual unknown.
runners_data.comment: Consistent filly who has won twice and finished second twice in her last four starts, and she has run over today's trip before; 126 lb from stall 15 and a rating of 102 place her mid-pack on paper, though her recent reliability makes her one to respect.

runners_data.name: Pivotal Attack
runners_data.note: Prominent-running 3yo for Joseph Murphy who won on Soft over 7f most recently and ran 4th on Good over 8f; the step up to 1m1f is new territory and his sim-going mark of 6/8 is modest, though Gary Carroll keeps the ride and he has placed or won in five consecutive starts.
runners_data.comment: Pivotal Attack arrives on the back of a win last time out, and her experience over today's trip and going is an asset; she returns after 30 days off in sound shape and looks capable of going well from stall four off 126 lb.

runners_data.name: Saga Gaga
runners_data.note: A natural prominent racer whose last two wins came over 10f and 12f on Good ground for M D O'Callaghan — her form figures read 7115 and she is clearly progressive; the field's pace congestion means she is likely squeezed out of her preferred front-rank position and will race mid-group, which blunts her effectiveness.
runners_data.comment: Ranked 13 of 15 on our figures, Saga Gaga is hard to fancy despite back-to-back wins two and three starts back; a fifth last time out and a lowly speed rating make her tough to recommend, though she has distance and going experience to call on.

runners_data.name: Sky Watch
runners_data.note: O'Callaghan's second string (hg:p) who has placed without winning in three of five recent starts and handles Good ground adequately; she races prominently but 0W0P at this level on similar going is not a compelling profile, and she is arguably better suited to a strongly-run race where she can track the pace without fighting for position.
runners_data.comment: Sky Watch has placed third twice in her last two starts but ranks 14th of 15 on our figures, making her very hard to fancy against this field; she has run over today's trip and going before, and her win in her last five starts shows she can find the line.

races.paceDynamic: Faiyum and Garden Party are the two confirmed front-runners in a 15-runner field, and with six horses wanting prominent positions there will be early competition for the front rank, ensuring an honest and sustained gallop over this 1m1f on Good ground at The Curragh. Faiyum (Colin Keane, 116 days off) will likely assert to lead with Garden Party (Wayne Lordan) pressing her, creating a genuine pace that compresses the midfield and stretches the field through the belly of the race. The congestion between second and fifth position — with Meriden, Miss Scott, Bosphorus Rose, Pivotal Attack and Thalara all wanting to be prominent — raises a real danger of scrimmaging and interference two to three furlongs out when the race begins to quicken. This shape most favours hold-up horses with a turn of foot who can exploit a fast-run race from off the pace — true closers like Sindria and Drop Dead Gorgeous are ideally profiled — but the field holds more front-running and prominent types than can all secure their natural positions, with Saga Gaga, Spicy Margarita and Della Pace the most likely to find themselves shuffled back out of role; Faiyum and Garden Party are best placed to actually control the shape from the front.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Lead, Closers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Faiyum and Garden Party drive a genuine gallop that strings the field out, setting it up for runners coming from off the pace.
scenarios.body: The front-runners burn each other off through an honest pace, leaving the prominent cluster struggling for cover late, while hold-up horses with a clean run deliver late power; the 1m1f trip at Curragh rewards those who travel into the race rather than fight for position.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Type Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the early contest for the lead moderates once Garden Party settles and the pace becomes controlled rather than truly punishing.
scenarios.body: A steady enough gallop over the first half allows a well-placed prominent horse to hold enough in reserve to kick off the turn, with the extra furlong beyond a mile rewarding those who get into the race early; congestion in the pack suits those who grab a clean position behind the pace.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If Faiyum asserts command early and Garden Party drops away or is outpaced, allowing the leader to dictate a controlled solo gallop.
scenarios.body: With Colin Keane able to set his own fractions unchallenged, Faiyum can conserve energy through the middle portion and produce a strong finish from a leader's position; her form pattern of winning when allowed to control tempo supports this shape.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos Suits Outsider
scenarios.trigger: If the six-horse scrum for prominent positions causes traffic incidents two furlongs out that disrupt the fancied runners' runs.
scenarios.body: A messy race with multiple horses changing position late can produce a gap for a horse finding herself on a clear rail, with the field's redistribution issues meaning several horses are out of position throughout; a horse at a longer price with pace to use from a good draw could benefit from the resulting disorder.

watchPoints.text: Faiyum and Garden Party — watch the battle for the lead in the opening two furlongs; if both commit fully, they risk burning each other off and handing the race to closers, but if one concedes early the shape changes entirely.

Prominent cluster (Meriden, Miss Scott, Bosphorus Rose, Pivotal Attack, Thalara) — six horses targeting the same three positions creates genuine collision risk between the 3f and 2f pole; horses drawn wide in this group should be monitored for being pushed wide entering the home straight.

Thalara — a 343-day absence is a serious flag despite her 2W5P record on Good going; watch her in the parade ring and early in the race for signs she has not come to hand after nearly a full year off.

Drop Dead Gorgeous — stepping up to 1m1f for the first time with Ryan Moore, which points to trainer confidence; watch whether she travels into the race smoothly as the trip will find her out if stamina is the limiting factor.

Saga Gaga and Della Pace — both are racing out of their natural position due to redistribution; watch where they actually settle at the start, as either finding their preferred spot would alter this race's shape and their individual prospects materially.

races.name: Tote Irish Cambridgeshire

runners_data.name: Big Gossey
runners_data.note: A nine-year-old hold-up specialist who has shown recent flat-track form over shorter trips; likely to be outpaced from the start of this mile on a day when the pace is not strong enough to set up a late rattle.
runners_data.comment: Big Gossey shaped well when second two starts back and has won twice in his last six starts, arriving fresh on 20 days' rest with experience of today's trip and going; the 142 lb burden is worth noting, but he heads the ratings as the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Hardy Warrior
runners_data.note: Drop back to a mile for Joseph O'Brien's three-year-old who has been running over ten furlongs recently; hold-up style and soft-ground form (hg: tv) are minor concerns on Good, but there is finishing ability here if the pace unfolds generously.
runners_data.comment: Hardy Warrior shaped with plenty of promise when third last time out and was a winner five starts back, bringing strong recent form into this having run over today's trip and going; the main risk is that he has not recaptured that winning thread in his last four outings.

runners_data.name: Ribee
runners_data.note: Prominent racer for Michael Mulvany who showed a return to form when second on the Curragh mile in similar conditions; Ben Coen in the saddle is a significant booking and the horse has course and going form to call upon.
runners_data.comment: Ribee showed his best when scoring five starts back, and that winning form combined with experience over today's trip and going keeps him very much in the picture from stall six off 133 lb; the worry is he has finished fifth or worse in three of his four most recent starts.

runners_data.name: Rahmi
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old hold-up type who has been well beaten in recent starts and arrives here at OR 97 without a win in this trip in current Going; the sim-going record (2W5P from 15) is the one encouragement.
runners_data.comment: Rahmi shaped with plenty of promise when second last time out, has experience of today's trip and going, and a rating of 102 puts him firmly in contention from stall four on a return 22 days later; the main concern is a trainer operating at just 3% over the last fortnight.

runners_data.name: Pierre Royal
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent performer at the Curragh mile for Adrian McGuinness who recorded a recent win over this course and distance; 7/7 sim-going record is striking and Adam Caffrey knows this horse well.
runners_data.comment: Pierre Royal won three starts back and was second two starts back, so he arrives in decent nick after 27 days off; he has run over today's trip and going before and carries 128 lb from stall 10, though a fourth last time out and a rating of 93 suggest he faces a stiff task against stronger rivals.

runners_data.name: Lord Massusus
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with no wins or places from ten starts on the Curragh mile at Good; the form string reads poorly and he arrives without obvious tactical advantages in this shape.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Lord Massusus at least returns on a manageable 27-day break with experience over today's trip and conditions, and a rating of 98 gives him fair claims from stall 11, though the 127 lb burden is a stern ask against this field.

runners_data.name: Loughrea
runners_data.note: The only confirmed front-runner in the field, trained and ridden by Andrew Slattery who has combined for three wins in 22 days; two recent wins at this course and distance make her the key pace-setter whose ability to control the tempo is central to how the entire race unfolds.
runners_data.comment: Loughrea arrives in cracking recent form — a winner last time out and two starts back, though he was only second three starts back and has had 44 days off the track since, which may blunt that sharpness slightly; experience over today's trip and going at least counts in his favour.

runners_data.name: Dos Mukasan
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up type who fades in the finish and carries a redistribution flag — placed in midfield on the map because the rear of the field is over-subscribed; his best form came on Fibresand and his Curragh record on Good gives little encouragement.
runners_data.comment: Four consecutive starts without troubling the judge since winning five starts back make Dos Mukasan hard to fancy at the foot of our rankings, and his speed figure of 75 underlines the concern; stall one and experience over today's trip are modest positives at best.

runners_data.name: Final Voyage
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse for J P Murtagh who landed a recent win over ten furlongs on Good ground; dropping back to a mile with a 7lb claimer (Jessica Maye) and held up in a race where the pace may not be strong enough to suit his pattern.
runners_data.comment: Second last time out suggests Final Voyage is finding his feet again, but the trainer's dire recent strike-rate — just one winner from 29 — is a notable concern, and he has been inconsistent in recent starts, with only one win in his last six.

runners_data.name: Booyea
runners_data.note: A natural hold-up horse carrying blinkers who is mapped to midfield due to the overcrowded rear of the field; the style fit discount (0.92) is warranted given he is unlikely to get the truly strong pace he needs, and his recent form at this distance on Good is modest.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked 13 of 18 on our figures, Booyea faces a stiff ask from stall 16 carrying 124 lb, and an eighth last time out does little to inspire confidence, though he has run over today's distance and going before.

runners_data.name: Hellorhighwater
runners_data.note: Unbeaten in two starts on Good or Good-to-soft over a mile, winning the same Curragh trip in August; 126-day absence is the only query, but Natalia Lupini has kept this horse fresh before and the prominent style suits this race shape perfectly.
runners_data.comment: Hellorhighwater arrives in decent nick with back-to-back wins and has run over today's trip and going, though 126 days off the track is a concern and his rating of 93 ranks him mid-pack in an 18-runner field.

runners_data.name: Manton Bay
runners_data.note: A three-year-old who has won and been placed at this trip on Good for David Marnane; his true hold-up style means he is nudged into midfield on the map (STYLE_FIT 0.90), though recent course form and Luke McAteer's claiming allowance keep him relevant.
runners_data.comment: Manton Bay won last time out and returns quickly on eight days' rest, with experience over today's trip and going in his favour; however, he finished eighth three starts back and is ranked towards the bottom of this field, so he faces a stiff ask from stall two off 123 lb.

runners_data.name: Kalir
runners_data.note: Dermot Weld's three-year-old has won his last two starts over this course and distance on Good ground and races prominently; the headgear flag (hg: p) suggests he needs to be produced with confidence, and this race shape suits him well if he can track the leader.
runners_data.comment: Kalir won his last two outings so arrives in form, but our figures rank him well below the field here, and a speed rating of 71 makes him hard to fancy at the weights despite his recent back-to-back victories.

runners_data.name: Playin Cool
runners_data.note: Prominent racer for John James Feane who has shown placing form at this trip; 51 days off the track and a modest OR of 84 make him vulnerable against better-credentialled prominent types in this field.
runners_data.comment: Playin Cool has shown he can mix it at this level, placing second and third in recent starts, but he is yet to win in his last five and returns after 51 days off, which adds a fitness query to his already inconsistent profile.

runners_data.name: Genuine Article
runners_data.note: A six-year-old hold-up type whose form figures in recent starts (0500) are discouraging; mapped into midfield due to redistribution, his true closer style is unlikely to be rewarded with a pace that favours those racing up with the running.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Genuine Article does at least bring distance and going experience to the table, and 27 days between runs suggests he arrives fresh; however, his recent string of unplaced efforts makes it hard to fancy him strongly from stall 13 off 119 lb.

runners_data.name: Slieve Binnian
runners_data.note: Prominent racer for David Marnane who has returned to form with a recent placing; the step back to a mile from longer trips and the sim-going record (2W3P) are modest, and Jamie Powell takes the ride in a competitive handicap.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts and ranked 16 of 18 on our figures, Slieve Binnian is hard to fancy, though he has run over today's trip and going before and returns on a quick 14-day turnaround in reasonable condition.

runners_data.name: Engines On
runners_data.note: Prominent type with blinkered headgear who was placed last time at this trip on Good; 76 days off the track and a declining OR at this trip make him difficult to recommend, though he gets the pace shape he needs.
runners_data.comment: Engines On has been unplaced in each of his last three starts and, ranked near the foot of the field on our figures, is hard to fancy at this stage; he does at least return to a familiar distance and going, and that winning run four starts back is a reminder he can find the line.

runners_data.name: Johnny Soda
runners_data.note: Three-year-old with two recent wins at the Curragh mile on Good ground, ridden by 7lb claimer Reese Holohan; his true hold-up style is mapped into midfield because the field is hold-up heavy, and the style fit discount (0.93) reflects that he may not get the truly strong gallop he needs to deliver his best.
runners_data.comment: Johnny Soda has won three times in his last six starts, with a second last time out following back-to-back wins, so the recent form reads well enough, but he is ranked 14th of 18 on our figures and faces a stiff ask at the weights carrying 119 lb from stall 18.

races.paceDynamic: Loughrea is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 18-runner mile handicap at the Curragh, and with no genuine rival to press her early, Andrew Slattery can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the front — a significant positional advantage in a field this size. The prominent types — Ribee, Pierre Royal, Hellorhighwater, Kalir, Playin Cool and Slieve Binnian — will jostle for the early slots behind her, creating a competitive but not frenetic early pace that should keep the tempo honest without turning it into a scramble. The field holds considerably more hold-up horses than the race shape can accommodate at the rear: Dos Mukasan, Booyea, Manton Bay, Genuine Article and Johnny Soda are all genuine closers who will be forced to travel wider in midfield than they would naturally prefer, compromising their finishing options. With a lone, uncontested leader setting a measured pace on Good ground, this race shape firmly favours prominent racers who can track Loughrea at close range and pounce in the straight — horses forced wide and deep from true hold-up positions face an uphill task against a pace that is unlikely to collapse sufficiently for them to mow down those ahead.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Loughrea Controls, Prominent Win
scenarios.trigger: If Loughrea gets a clean lead and sets a measured pace that allows prominent trackers to travel comfortably before asserting.
scenarios.body: Loughrea dictates from the front on her own terms while Hellorhighwater, Kalir and Pierre Royal track in the slipstream, poised to challenge two furlongs out; on a sound surface with no pace pressure, the controlled gallop rewards horses who travel prominently without burning energy in traffic. Prominent types get first run on a field where the genuine hold-up horses are forced out of their natural rhythm, arriving too late.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Loughrea Completes the Hat-Trick
scenarios.trigger: If Loughrea is allowed an even softer lead than expected and the prominent pack fails to apply meaningful pressure until too late.
scenarios.body: Having won her last two starts over course and distance, Loughrea slots into a rhythm unchallenged and builds enough of a buffer turning in that the prominent chasers cannot reel her in; on Good going where she has proven her class, this is a live scenario, particularly if the jockeys behind misjudge the pace. Her trainer-jockey combination running her in-house adds further tactical cohesion.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Closers Storm Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace quickens sharply early as multiple prominent types jostle for position, causing the race to be run at a genuinely strong tempo that breaks the field apart.
scenarios.body: A faster-than-expected early fractions would drain the prominent runners turning for home and open a late gap for midfield-to-hold-up types who are conserved; Hardy Warrior, Final Voyage and Ribee all have the profile to pick up late ground if the pace is genuine. The redistribution of true hold-up types into midfield marginally aids this scenario, though the controlled nature of Loughrea's expected lead limits the probability.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: True Hold-Up Types Land Late
scenarios.trigger: If a genuinely strong pace develops early and the field strings out, allowing horses ridden from off the pace to find clear daylight late.
scenarios.body: This scenario requires a faster race than the single front-runner is likely to generate, and the redistributed hold-up horses — Dos Mukasan, Johnny Soda, Booyea — would need to overcome both their compromised starting positions and the fact that the pace is unlikely to be strong enough to fully suit them. The low STYLE_FIT scores for these redistributed runners underline why this scenario carries the lowest weight.

watchPoints.text: Hellorhighwater is unbeaten at this course and distance on Good ground and races from a prominent position that suits this race shape — watch for Wayne Lordan positioning him just behind Loughrea from the outset.

Kalir has won his last two starts at this exact course and trip on Good going for Dermot Weld — if Chris Hayes secures a prominent pitch at the top of the straight, he becomes a serious winning threat.

Loughrea will attempt to lead from flag to finish as the only genuine front-runner — watch whether Andrew Slattery is allowed to stride clear unchallenged or whether prominent rivals push forward to press her, which would fundamentally change the race shape.

Johnny Soda and Manton Bay are both genuine hold-up horses mapped into midfield due to redistribution — watch whether their jockeys (both claim allowances) try to force an earlier position than natural, which could crowd the inside rail early.

Pierre Royal's 7/7 record on Good or Good-to-soft at the Curragh is worth noting — if the prominent pack is large and competitive, he has the course and going profile to emerge as the each-way danger at a bigger price.

races.name: Holden Plant Rentals Apprentice Handicap

runners_data.name: Gerrit's Gem
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse for Coogan (0/2 in 14 days) who has finished 7th, 13th, and 10th in recent 6f Good ground runs — poor sim-going record of 1 win in 10 is not encouraging, and finding a clear run through 21 runners from the rear is a major ask.

runners_data.name: Faoladh
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner for Slattery (3/22 in 14 days) who most recently won over 7f on Good; dropping to 6f is a concern given four consecutive runs beyond 7f, but the horse has the freshness of a 28-day break and Ava Maher's 7lb claim could offset the weight disadvantage.
runners_data.comment: Faoladh won last time out and has experience of today's trip and conditions, but two unplaced efforts before that run and a tall weight of 141 lb from stall 18 give his supporters pause for thought.

runners_data.name: Naoi
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse who has placed in four of five runs on Good ground including a recent 7f Good win, making him one of the few true closers in this field with proven ability at the trip and going; the 9-day turnaround for McCreery's yard (3/18 in 14 days) is a positive and Sam Coen gets on well with the horse.
runners_data.comment: Won last time out — a win nine days ago on a quick turnaround — and she has run over today's trip and going before, which helps; however, that eighth two starts back is a concern, and ranked eighth of 21 here, she faces a stiff task carrying 140 lb.

runners_data.name: Flaming Rib
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old hold-up type with a visor, trained by McGuinness (4/24 in 14 days); sim-going record shows zero wins and zero places from six runs on similar ground, and recent finishes of 7th and 8th at 6f-7f suggest this horse is operating below the level needed to compete here.
runners_data.comment: Flaming rib is winless in his last five starts, yet our rating of 82 marks him out as the standout in a field of 21, and he has experience of both today's trip and going; the risk is that his recent finishing positions — seventh and eighth in back-to-back outings — make the turnaround a significant ask.

runners_data.name: Poweracclaim
runners_data.note: Prominent racer for JP Murtagh (1/29 in 14 days) who has placed in two of five recent runs over 6f on Good — a 3rd and a 4th in the last two — and is 49 days since last run, but the consistent position just off the pace suits this race shape precisely.
runners_data.comment: Poweracclaim caught the eye with a third last time out and has run over today's trip and going, while our rating puts him comfortably clear of his official mark — a strong case for a big run; the main worry is 49 days off and a trainer firing at just 3% lately.

runners_data.name: Four Blondes
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse for O'Sullivan (0/20 in 14 days) who has a recent 6th and 5th at 6f on Good; the 7-day turnaround is quick and the trainer's form is cold, but sim-going record of 13 runs with no wins and 2 places limits expectations.
runners_data.comment: Four Blondes has run over today's trip and going, and her rating of 77 — ranking her third in a field of 21 — makes her a leading threat on a quick seven-day turnaround; the concern is a trainer who is yet to land a winner in the last 14 days.

runners_data.name: Lethimfly
runners_data.note: Hold-up type trained by Keane (1/7 in 14 days) who has been running over 5f in recent starts — the step up to 6f is a positive given those 5f runs suggest no shortage of pace — but 0 wins from 10 sim-going runs and a 56-day absence raise fitness questions.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Lethimfly does at least hold experience over today's trip and going, and a second four starts back shows he can get competitive; however, three consecutive unplaced efforts since, plus 56 days off the track and a hefty 135 lb to carry, make improvement hard to predict.

runners_data.name: Call The Cavalry
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse from Timmons (0/7 in 14 days) who has run exclusively at Dundalk on Tapeta and Fibresand; all five career runs are on artificial surfaces and there is no turf form whatsoever to assess — going preference is genuinely unknown.
runners_data.comment: Call The Cavalry is winless in his last five starts, with his best recent effort a second four starts back, and an unplaced run last time out does little to inspire; experience over today's trip and a quick 14-day turnaround offer some encouragement, though his rating of 62 suggests he faces a stiff task from 21 runners.

runners_data.name: Rosato
runners_data.note: Prominent-to-prominent racer with a headgear change (p — first time?) who has two 2nd-place finishes from five 6f Good runs at this course for Charles Weld; the 7-day turnaround and sim-going record of 1 win and 3 places from 15 runs make this horse one of the more convincing positive profiles for the race shape.
runners_data.comment: Twice a runner-up in her last six starts yet winless in that spell, Rosato arrives on a quick seven-day turnaround with experience over today's trip and going, though carrying 132 lb from stall 16 on a modest official mark of 62 leaves her with plenty to find.

runners_data.name: Coincidental Glory
runners_data.note: Prominent racer for McGuinness (4/24 in 14 days) who finished 2nd at 6f on Good recently and has placed twice in similar conditions; the 3-year-old has held a challenging position in recent races and the apprentice Reese Holohan's 2lb claim is a minor asset.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, though a second three starts back and a third four starts back hint at ability, while experience over today's trip and going offers some comfort; the 131 lb burden from stall 10 looks the main obstacle to reversing recent fortunes.

runners_data.name: Top Biller
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner for Hogan (2/23 in 14 days) who was placed in two of five recent runs at 6f on Good including wins and 2nd places — but the 72-day absence is the longest of any confirmed pace-setter and fitness after that layoff is a real concern before asking the horse to lead 21 rivals.
runners_data.comment: Top Biller is winless in his last six starts, and a ranking of 19 from 21 on our figures makes him hard to fancy here; 72 days off adds a fitness query, though he has run over today's trip and going before and the two seconds in recent starts offer some crumb of comfort.

runners_data.name: Apothic Red
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with a visor for McCourt (0/14 in 14 days) who recorded a 2nd over 6f on Good most recently; the 3-year-old is relatively lightly raced with only 5 runs, and the apprentice Sadhbh Tormey carries a 7lb claim which gives a weight advantage in a competitive handicap.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Apothic Red at least shaped with some promise when second last time out, and he has run over today's trip and going before; carrying 128 lb from stall eight, he rates a shade better than his official mark of 61 suggests, though consistency remains the question.

runners_data.name: Dervo Annie
runners_data.note: Naturally a hold-up horse for O'Connell (0/6 in 14 days), but the sheer volume of hold-up types in this field means the horse is mapped to midfield and will likely race out of role; recent 7th and 6th over longer trips on Good suggest form is moving in the wrong direction, and the style fit of 0.93 tempers expectations.
runners_data.comment: Dervo Annie showed her best when winning and finishing second in earlier starts, but a seventh and sixth in her last two runs suggest she's gone off the boil; she has experience of today's trip and conditions, though a mark of 61 and draw seven make her a tough each-way proposition.

runners_data.name: Tawaazon
runners_data.note: Third confirmed front-runner — a tie-back (tb) headgear horse for Kinsella (0/2 in 14 days) who has been running over 5f recently; stepping up to 6f against two other pace-setters at age 8, with only 1 win from 13 similar-going runs, means Tawaazon is more likely to be a pace contributor than a winner.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Tawaazon heads here just six days after his latest fifth, and while he has run over today's trip and going before, a rating of 63 from stall six at 126 lb leaves him with plenty to find against a competitive field.

runners_data.name: Caffu Zafeen
runners_data.note: A true hold-up horse that the field density pushes into a midfield mapping — Paul Flynn's runner (1/22 in 14 days) has form of 0009 and recent finishes of 9th, 11th, 15th, and 18th; the style fit discount of 0.92 reflects both the redistribution and the deeply uninspiring recent form.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, with three unplaced efforts sandwiching a ninth last time out, Caffu Zafeen is hard to fancy from stall 19 on a 5% trainer strike rate; he has run over today's trip and going, but little else in the profile compels.

runners_data.name: I'm Spartacus
runners_data.note: Prominent racer for McGuinness (4/24 in 14 days) whose form reads 160480 — a win at 6f followed by a string of poor efforts; the 6-day turnaround is very quick and sim-going record of 1 win and 1 place from 15 runs does not inspire confidence at this class.
runners_data.comment: A winner six starts back, I'm Spartacus has been largely out of the cards since, finishing eighth two starts back and unplaced last time out just six days ago; the quick turnaround and a rating 13 points above his official mark offer some hope, but the recent form makes belief a stretch.

runners_data.name: Simmering Seas
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse whose natural position is unavailable in this field, pushing the horse into midfield where the style fit drops to 0.91; Flynn's 3-year-old (2/8 in 14 days) has a 4th and 2nd over 5f on Good recently, suggesting ability, but racing out of role in a 21-runner handicap is a significant disadvantage.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked 16 of 21 on our figures, Simmering Seas is hard to fancy despite her experience over today's trip and going; a second two starts back is the best she offers, and six days since her last run at least suggests she arrives fresh.

runners_data.name: Strikepoint
runners_data.note: Only three career runs and a fade-in-finish flag make this 3-year-old extremely hard to assess — all runs have been at 5f-6f and the horse has never finished better than 7th; naturally a hold-up type operating out of role in a busy field, with the style fit of 0.90 the lowest in the race and the inexperience compounding the tactical problem.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last three starts, with a ninth last time out the chief concern, Strikepoint heads here 14 days later rated just 54 officially and ranked 17 of 21 on our figures; experience over today's trip and going, plus a 14-day turnaround, are slim pickings for optimism from stall 17.

runners_data.name: Fontaine Khaled
runners_data.note: Harty's 3-year-old hold-up horse (0/7 in 14 days) who finished 5th at 7f Good most recently with a record showing 3rd at 7f Good as a highlight; the horse is mapped to midfield through redistribution but has enough staying power at 7f to suggest 6f may be sharp — not ideal either way.
runners_data.comment: Ranked 18 of 21 on our figures, Fontaine Khaled makes this very difficult to fancy — winless in her last six starts, with a fifth last time out and only a solitary third three starts back to offer any encouragement, though she has run over today's trip and going and returns on a reasonable 22-day break.

runners_data.name: Another Nice'day
runners_data.note: Carried a headgear change (p) and has a 4th at 5f Good recently with one win over 5f Good in career — the Lynch yard (0/2 in 14 days) is cold and this horse is a natural hold-up type pushed into a midfield role by the field dynamics; stepping to 6f from repeated 5f runs could be a positive if the style displacement can be managed.
runners_data.comment: Ranked near the foot of the field on our figures and carrying 119 lb from stall 15, Another Nice'day faces a stiff ask, his sole win in his last six starts coming three runs back amid a largely inconsistent recent record, though he has run over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Pure Valour
runners_data.note: The lowest-rated horse in the field (OR=44) for Coogan (0/2 in 14 days) with a tie-back headgear flag, whose recent history shows 6f Good finishes alongside 8f, 10f, and 8f runs — a horse clearly placed here on the lowest possible mark; naturally a hold-up type mapped to midfield, and the style fit of 0.90 combined with no wins or places on similar going from 5 runs makes this a very difficult proposition.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Pure Valour faces a stiff task here; she does arrive on a sharp 13-day turnaround with experience of today's trip and going to her name, but that is the limit of the encouragement.

races.paceDynamic: Faoladh, Top Biller, and Tawaazon are all confirmed front-runners in a 21-runner field over 6f at the Curragh on Good ground, guaranteeing a strong, pressured gallop from the outset with no prospect of a false pace. The three leaders will push each other through the early and middle sectionals, compressing the race into a stamina-sapping contest where horses who settle behind the speed and sustain their effort into the final furlong will be best placed. The redistribution of genuine hold-up types — Dervo Annie, Strikepoint, Simmering Seas, Fontaine Khaled, Another Nice'day, Caffu Zafeen, and Pure Valour — into the midfield zone reflects the reality that they cannot access their natural rear position in this traffic, and several of those horses will be racing out of role. This race shape strongly favours a prominent racer who travels economically just off the pace without getting caught in the front-running battle, then sustains a finish when the leaders inevitably tie up in the closing stages.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If the three front-runners burn each other off through a searingly fast early pace, setting up the race for a prominent racer who travels just behind the battle.
scenarios.body: Faoladh, Top Biller, and Tawaazon will have done significant damage to each other by the 2f pole, leaving the race open for a horse that has settled on the pace without leading — Poweracclaim and Rosato both carry prominent profiles and have proven 6f Good course form.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Survives Pressure
scenarios.trigger: If one of the three front-runners gets a workable lead, controls the fractions, and proves strong enough to hold on despite the strong pace.
scenarios.body: Faoladh is the most likely candidate given a recent win and the best form profile of the three, and if apprentice Ava Maher can slot Faoladh into a rhythm rather than a war, the horse has the class to hold every challenger. Top Biller also has a win at this course on Good ground and could benefit if Tawaazon burns out early.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is truly extreme and the field strings out, creating a genuine gap for a deep closer to finish powerfully through beaten horses.
scenarios.body: Naoi is the most convincingly capable hold-up horse whose form suggests real ability on Good ground, but several redistributed horses — Dervo Annie, Simmering Seas — are racing out of their natural position and will struggle to access the back of the field, making this scenario dependent on fewer genuinely suited closers than it appears.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Delivery At Odds
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves more honest than extreme, and a midfield type who avoids early trouble delivers a clean run to the front inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Coincidental Glory has shown a 2nd at 6f on Good and a consistent prominent-to-midfield profile, and a clean draw with a capable apprentice could allow a well-timed challenge; Apothic Red also has a recent 2nd over 6f on Good ground and carries a manageable weight.
